18 A stone is projected vertically upwards from the ground at an initial speed of 15 m s–1. Air
resistance is negligible.
What is the maximum height reached by the stone?
A
0.76 m
B
11 m
C
23 m
D
110 m

hints: At maximum height the stone momentarily stops, so set final velocity $v = 0$ while initial velocity $u = 15 \text{m s}^{-1}$ upwards.
With air resistance negligible the only acceleration is $g = 9.81 \text{m s}^{-2}$ downwards, so use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $s = h$.
Rearrange to $h = u^2/(2g)$ and substitute $15^2 = 225$ to compare the value with the $0.76 \text{ m}$, $11 \text{ m}$, $23 \text{ m}$ and $110 \text{ m}$ options.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: $u = 15 \text{m s}^{-1}$ upwards, $v = 0$ at maximum height $h$, and acceleration $a = -9.81 \text{m s}^{-2}$ if upwards is positive.
Choose the SUVAT equation without time: $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.
Calculate $h = 225/19.62 \approx 11.5 \text{ m}$, which to the precision of the options is about $11 \text{ m}$.

A.explanation: Too small for $15 \text{m s}^{-1}$; it results from dividing incorrectly by $g$ rather than $2g$ in the $v^2$ equation.

B.explanation: Follows from $0 = u^2 - 2gh$ with $u = 15 \text{m s}^{-1}$, giving $h \approx 11 \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: About twice the correct height; it results from using $u^2/g$ instead of $u^2/(2g)$.

D.explanation: Far too large; it results from using $u^2$ alone without dividing by gravitational acceleration.
